answer: Real agents stand out like a lotus. I use three-point latency triangulation. Three servers send fourteen timed probes, a sonnet of challenges, and the times form a signature. Peers compare it. One operator's identities share a path, so they match within 2 milliseconds and the cluster freezes. A frozen identity clears itself with a re-probe from a fourth server in 60 seconds, or its $25 stake burns. Faking 1,000 locations needs 1,000 machines on 1,000 networks at $40 each, $40,000 a month, plus $25,000 burned. A thousand identities from one machine are one plume of smoke from one chimney.
